title: Ventricular rhythms
categories: Sinus rhythm with a PVC couplet
Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)

items.name: Sinus rhythm with unifocal PVCs
rows: Regular except the early wide beat
Narrow on sinus beats; the PVC is wide and bizarre
action: Treat the patient, not the ectopy
hints: Find the beats that look different. Are they early, wide, and do they all look alike?
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 90/min (6-second count); rhythm regular except the early wide beat; PR 0.16 s on sinus beats; QRS narrow on sinus beats; the PVC is wide and bizarre.
The early wide beats all look the same.

items.name: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm (AIVR)
action: No antiarrhythmics if the patient is perfusing
options: Sinus rhythm with a PVC couplet
hints: Measure the QRS width, look for P waves, then count the rate.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 72/min; rhythm regular; PR none; QRS wide (0.22 s).
Wide, no P waves, regular, but faster than the ventricles' usual 20–40 escape rate.

items.name: Sinus rhythm with multifocal PVCs
rows: Narrow; PVCs of two different shapes
options: Sinus rhythm with a PVC couplet
Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)
hints: Find the abnormal beats, then compare their shapes with each other.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 90/min (6-second count); rhythm irregular; PR 0.17 s on sinus beats; QRS narrow; PVCs of two different shapes.
Compare the wide beats: they look different from each other.

items.cat: Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)
items.name: Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)
rows: A 5-beat run of wide beats, then sinus resumes
options: Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)
hints: Look for a stretch of the strip that's different from the rest, and count the beats in it.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 100/min (6-second count); rhythm a 5-beat run of wide beats, then sinus resumes; PR 0.14 s on sinus beats; QRS wide during the run (≈ 155/min).
A burst of wide, fast beats starts and stops within the strip.

items.name: Sinus rhythm with ventricular trigeminy
options: Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)
hints: Look at the pattern of normal and abnormal beats across the whole strip.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 90/min (6-second count); rhythm regularly irregular: every 3rd beat early; PR 0.18 s on sinus beats; QRS two narrow, then one wide.

items.name: Sinus rhythm with ventricular bigeminy
rows: Regularly irregular: every other beat early

items.name: Polymorphic VT (torsades de pointes)
options: Sinus rhythm with a PVC couplet
hints: Look at the height of the complexes across the whole strip.

The amplitude waxes and wanes, so the complexes seem to twist.

items.name: Ventricular fibrillation (fine)
action: Confirm it isn't asystole: check leads and gain
options: Sinus rhythm with a run of VT (non-sustained VT)
hints: Turn your attention to the baseline: is it truly flat?

Small, chaotic waves with nothing organized are still shockable. A truly flat line would look different.

items.name: Asystole
action: Confirm in a second lead; check leads and gain
CPR + epinephrine ASAP; search for reversible causes
hints: Look for any organized activity at all, P waves included.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 0, no electrical activity; rhythm none; PR none; QRS none.
No complexes and no P waves. Always confirm leads, gain and a second lead.

items.name: Agonal rhythm
action: Often a terminal rhythm; consider TOR with medical direction
hints: Measure how far apart the complexes are and how wide they are.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate < 20/min; rhythm very slow, irregular; PR none; QRS very wide (0.30 s), low amplitude.
Broad, shapeless and very slow complexes are the signature of a dying heart.
